root_cause.text: `__xfrm_state_delete()` in `net/xfrm/xfrm_state.c` used mutable value fields (`x->km.seq` and `x->id.spi`) and unconditional `hlist_del_rcu()` calls to decide and perform removal from xfrm hash lists, so a state could be unlinked twice or from an already-unhashed list, causing writes through `LIST_POISON` and slab-use-after-free/OOB corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `hlist_del_rcu(&x->bydst/byrc/byseq/byspi)` to `hlist_del_init_rcu()` and replaces `if (x->km.seq)` / `if (x->id.spi)` with `if (!hlist_unhashed(...))`, matching the CVE text that “a second __xfrm_state_delete() on the same object writes through LIST_POISON pprev” and that value-based predicates could “skip-or-hit the byspi unhash inconsistently with whether x is actually on the list.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix xfrm state deletion to safely unlink hash nodes only when linked and reinitialize them after removal.
intent_record.what: In __xfrm_state_delete(), the code changes hlist removals for bydst, bysrc, byseq, and byspi from hlist_del_rcu() to hlist_del_init_rcu(), and replaces conditional checks on x->km.seq and x->id.spi with hlist_unhashed() checks before deleting byseq and byspi. The state_cache and state_cache_input deletions remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This makes the deleted xfrm_state's hash-list nodes explicitly reinitialized after removal, preventing stale hashed state from persisting in those links. The new hlist_unhashed() guards ensure deletion is only attempted when the node is actually linked, which avoids relying on unrelated fields like seq or spi and makes repeated or partial deletion states safer to handle.

grouping_result.intent: Fix xfrm state deletion to safely unlink hash nodes only when linked and reinitialize them after removal.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the xfrm state deletion bug by making hash-node unlinking conditional on linkage and reinitializing nodes after removal, which matches the root cause of unsafe repeated/invalid hlist deletions leading to corruption.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally unlinks the by-destination hash node, which can be unsafe if the node is already unhashed or was never linked, matching the double-unlink / LIST_POISON corruption root cause.
This is another unconditional hash-list deletion on a mutable state object; if the node is already removed, it can trigger invalid list writes and corruption.
The deletion is guarded only by the mutable field x->km.seq rather than actual linkage state, so it can attempt to remove an already-unhashed node or skip proper unlink tracking.
This uses the mutable SPI value to decide removal and performs an unconditional deletion, which can lead to double-unlink or invalid memory writes if the node is already detached.
The decision to delete byseq based on a mutable value field is directly implicated in the bug: the field may no longer reflect whether the hlist node is linked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional unlink of the by-destination hash node can run even when the node is already unhashed, matching the double-unlink / LIST_POISON corruption root cause.
This unconditional deletion of the by-source hash node can corrupt list state if the node was already removed, leading to invalid writes through poisoned list pointers.
This condition uses a mutable sequence field to decide whether to delete the by-sequence node, so it may not reflect actual linkage and can permit stale or repeated unlinking.
This deletion is driven by the mutable x->km.seq check rather than the node's linkage state, so it can attempt to unlink an already-unhashed list node.
This unconditional unlink of the by-SPI node can execute even after the node has already been detached, causing the same LIST_POISON/slab corruption issue.
